spec.name: Trend v31
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.0, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 16%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.05 to 2.04 (change -0.01).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.05 to 2.05. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.03 (as submitted, 8 bps: 2.05); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.05 against 2.05 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 2.92 against 2.05 in research, a gap of -0.87.
The best year gives 33% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 221%; Sharpe is 7.81 in calm and -8.53 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 5 distinct specs; the best of 5 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.07, so the claimed 2.00 becomes 1.93 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.11 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.05, 95th percentile 0.53).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.05 to as low as 1.69 (as low as 1.81 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 20% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 18% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Paper trading only: soft test damaging (regime_split EX-6).
